Admission and enrollment
Note: The information on this page applies to applications for the academic year 2027–2028.
English proficiency requirements
English proficiency requirements
To successfully participate in a TU/e program, you must be proficient in English. TU/e accepts the following English language proficiency test results:
TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language)
Starting January 21, 2026, TOEFL will update their iBT test, introducing enhancements to the test's security infrastructure, testing experience, and scoring scale. From this date, students will receive four section scores and an overall score on a 1-6 scale.
For TU/e's language requirements this means:
TOEFL test reports obtained before January 21, 2026:
Minimum overall score: 90
Minimum score per section: 21
Only TOEFL internet-based test (iBT) is accepted (home edition or at a test centre)
All scores must be from one test date
MyBest Scores is not accepted
TOEFL test reports obtained from January 21, 2026:
Minimum overall score: 4,5
Minimum score per section: 4,5
Only TOEFL internet-based test (iBT) is accepted (home edition or at a test centre)
All scores must be from one test date
MyBest Scores is not accepted
IELTS (Academic version)
Minimum overall score: 6.5
Minimum score per section: 6.0
All scores must be from one test date
IELTS online test is not accepted
IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted
University of Cambridge
C2 Proficiency (CPE): overall score 180, minimum of 169 per section, or
C1 Advanced Certificate (CAE): overall score 176, minimum of 169 per section
All scores must be from one test date
LanguageCert Academic
Minimum overall score: 70
Minimum score per section: 65
All scores must be from one test date
Online tests are not accepted
Pearson PTE Academic
Minimum overall score: 61
Minimum score per section: 46
All scores must be from one test date
Online tests are not accepted
Note: No other language tests are accepted. Test results must be no older than 2 years.
Submitting scores
It is mandatory to upload your official English language test score report in the online application form. Please note that it may take up to six weeks for some test centers to issue official results after you take the test. We strongly recommend scheduling and registering for your chosen test well in advance to ensure timely submission.
While exact timelines may vary, typical result release times are:
IELTS: 5–13 days
TOEFL: 4–8 days
Cambridge: 2–6 weeks
PTE Pearson: within 2 days
LanguageCert: around 7 days
Please check the official website of your test provider for the most accurate and up-to-date information. We must be able to verify your test results before the final application deadline. In addition to uploading your score report, we will verify your results using:
TRF number (IELTS)
Appointment number (TOEFL)
Verification number (Cambridge)
Score Report Code (PTE Pearson)
Candidate number (LanguageCert)
Exemptions from the English language tests
You are exempt from submitting an English test if you meet one of the following criteria:
Completed Dutch pre-university education (VWO)
Hold an ASO diploma from Flanders
Hold an IB or EB diploma with English as the sole language of instruction
IB: If not fully in English, exemption is possible with English A HL with a minimum score of 5.
EB: If not fully in English, exemption is possible with English Language 1 or 2.
Completed the entire high school education at an accredited USA high school located outside the USA (a high school degree obtained via online education does not qualify for an exemption).
Students who hold the nationality of Australia, Canada, Ireland, New-Zealand, United Kingdom, and the United States
Completed a 4-year HBO bachelor's degree in the Netherlands, with English as the sole language of instruction (demonstrated or indicated by the program).
Completed the entire bachelor's degree or the last 3 years of their High School in: Australia, Canada, Ireland, New-Zealand, United Kingdom, or the United States
Completed the full British curriculum (GCSE and A-levels) at an international/British school outside the United Kingdom.
No other exemptions are possible.
Dutch proficiency requirements
If you are applying for a Dutch-taught program at TU/e and were not previously educated in Dutch at a Dutch VWO (pre-university education) or HBO (University of Higher Professional Education also called University of Applied Sciences), you must submit proof of Dutch proficiency.
Accepted tests:
Dutch State Examination NT2-II
Certificate of Dutch as a Foreign Language (CNaVT) - Level STRT or EDUP.
Dutch State Examination NT2-II:
Apply via a recognized language institute (e.g. James Boswell Instituut or Tilburg University Language Centre)
Register for the exam via DUO, the Dutch student registration office
You may enroll for the TU/e program, after passing the NT2-II exam if conditionally admitted
Certificate of Dutch as a Foreign Language (level STRT or EDUP)
Register for an exam via the examiner who sends the registration forms to the CNaVT secretary until March, 15th
Find exam partners on the CNaVT website
Exams are held in the first half of May ( http://cnavt.org/en/introduction)
You may enroll for the TU/e program after obtaining the certificate if conditionally admitted
Exemptions
You have Dutch nationality
Completed Dutch VWO or HBO education with Dutch as the sole language of instruction
Hold an ASO diploma from Flanders
Hold an International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma with Dutch B Higher Level (HL) or Dutch A Standard Level or Higher Level (SL/HL).
